metadata.title: Claude Connectors
metadata.purpose: Introduce Claude Connectors, tour 9 favorites, and teach the three rules for when NOT to use them — especially the token-burning trap of leaving all connectors on by default.

props.command: What is: Don't Leave Them All On?

beats.narration_text: Jambo. This is Liam, in for Bear. What if you never had to tab out of Claude to check email, meetings, or your CRM? Claude Connectors. One-click bridges to every app you already use. But there's one rule most people miss.

props.ask: What's pending in my Gmail inbox from this week?
props.answer_preview: Claude reads your actual Gmail. Zero copy-pastes.

beats.narration_text: A Connector is a one-click bridge between Claude and an app you already pay for. Claude has hundreds of them. You're probably using none. Turn one on: open Claude, hit the plus icon in the chat bar, find Connectors, toggle it on for that conversation. That's it.

beats.narration_text: Nine favorites. Granola for meeting transcripts — ask Claude to summarize all of last week's meetings without opening a single dashboard. HubSpot or Salesforce — ask Claude what's the common thread in your last five closed deals. Notion for your team knowledge base. Microsoft 365 — one toggle, four apps: Teams, Outlook, Calendar, OneDrive. Slack for thread summaries and action items. Google Drive to push Claude's output directly into a spreadsheet. Gamma for on-brand slides in seconds. Gmail — save the five replies as drafts directly in Gmail, not just in the chat.

beats.narration_text: But here are three rules for when NOT to use them. Rule one: don't leave them all on by default. Every connector you load burns tokens before you type a single word. Treat the toggle bar like a kitchen tap — on per chat, off per chat. Rule two: don't use connectors for creative work. When you're writing, you want a clean room. Slack noise, Gmail noise, Notion noise pollutes the output. Every connector off for writing. Always. Rule three: don't grant write access until you trust the read flow. Read-only first. Watch how Claude uses it for a week. Then grant write.

beats.narration_text: The write-access rule deserves emphasis. Most data accidents happen on day one when someone enables a connector with full write access and asks Claude to clean up their Drive. Read-only for a week. Every time.

blocks.text: Most data accidents happen day one with write access enabled

items.title: Verify behavior before granting write access

card.sub: Most data accidents happen on day one. Read-only for a full week before granting write access.

beats.narration_text: If you want to build your own connector — a custom MCP server pointing at your internal database, your private wiki, that spreadsheet you've kept for three years — a connector is just an MCP server with a public URL. Your tech team can ship one in a few hours.

card.sub: A custom connector is an MCP server with a public URL. Point it at any system you control.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick three connectors only. My recommended starter stack: your meeting notes tool, your email, your team channel. Enable them one at a time. Run each for a full day before adding the next.
